note: Every magnitude here is a published measurement. Nothing is derived from orbital geometry, and an object with no measurement is not offered.

standardMagnitudeSource.citation: McCants, M. — Quicksat intrinsic magnitude file (qs.mag), 14 September 2020, https://mmccants.org/programs/
standardMagnitudeSource.convention: Visual magnitude at 1000 km range and 50 per cent illumination, which is a phase angle of 90 degrees.

spacecraft.name: International Space Station
spacecraft.appearance: A steady white point, brighter than any star, crossing the sky in a few minutes without blinking. Aircraft have flashing lights and change course; this does neither.

starlink.citation: Mallama, A., Cole, R. E., Respler, J., Harrington, S., Lee, R. and Worley, A. (2024) — The Brightness of Starlink Mini Satellites During Orbit-Raising, arXiv:2405.12007
starlink.convention: Mean apparent magnitude adjusted to a uniform distance of 1000 km. Distance is normalised out; phase angle is not, so only range may be applied to it.
